title: tailored-observability-iac-adapter-for-private-vpc
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers need an opinionated Terraform module that wires up a production-ready observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana + OpenTelemetry Collector + log shippers) with safe lifecycle hooks for rolling upgrades and health gating. Existing modules are either too generic (manual wiring, fragile upgrades) or tightly coupled to our hosted defaults.

Goal: Deliver a Terraform module (redwood_vpc_observability_adapter) that packages deployment patterns, upgrade probes, and idempotent configuration so Platform teams can enable observability in customer VPCs with predictable SLOs and zero-surprise upgrades.

Scope: Module should provision helm releases (k8s) or manifest-level resources in customer clusters via our IaC patterns, expose canary upgrade hooks, liveness/readiness probes for critical components, pre-upgrade drain/replica checks for Prometheus and OTLP statefulsets, and a logship sidecar daemonset pattern with configurable backpressure and retention. It must integrate with our existing VPC networking TF modules and KMS integrations for Grafana secrets.

Out of scope: Grafana dashboards authoring (we provide a template import path), custom scraping rules per-app (left to platform-onboarding templates).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can be applied to a test VPC and produce Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector, and a logship daemonset with sane defaults
Module exposes upgrade_lock and canary_replicas inputs and honors them during terraform apply via lifecycle hooks
Rolling upgrade plan does not drop metrics ingestion for more than 30s in default configuration (measured in test harness)
Pre-upgrade health checks run and block upgrade if >10% pods in critical state, with clear error messages
Module includes example usage (inputs/outputs) and a minimal GitHub action that runs tf plan + integration smoke tests
Documentation page in Confluence with architecture diagram, upgrade runbook, and troubleshooting checklist
testing_instructions: Spin up a disposable test VPC using infra/tf/demos/test-vpc - apply with module enabled
Run ./scripts/smoke.sh which deploys a test app that emits metrics and logs, then verify ingestion in Grafana and Prometheus (dashboard URL returned in outputs)
Execute upgrade scenario: change module version input and run terraform apply; observe canary_replicas path and pre-upgrade blockers
Run pager simulation: mark one Prometheus replica NotReady and ensure upgrade is gated
updates: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: scoped module interface. Decided to use Helm releases behind the module with an option to render manifests for air-gapped installs. (Asha)

2025-02-20 - Spike complete: OTLP collector statefulset needed sticky volumes for batching; we moved batching storage to emptyDir when in stateless mode to avoid cross-cluster retention issues. Trade-off: emptyDir loses in-flight batches on node restart but simplifies upgrades. (Gabriel)

2025-02-27 - Review feedback from Security: require KMS-backed secrets for Grafana admin and alertmanager webhooks. Added optional kms_key_id input and validation in pre-apply hook. (security@redwood)

2025-03-01 - Implementation: added pre-upgrade probe that queries /-/healthy on Prometheus and chunks scrape targets to avoid overload during rollout. Introduced canary_replicas input and default 1 replica for canary. (PR #1429)

2025-03-04 - Integration smoke tests flaky on logship backpressure under high log rates. Mitigation: add configurable max_buffer_size with default conservative value and add tuning guidance to docs. Follow-up: benchmark under customer workload next cycle. (Gabriel)
2025-03-06 - QA sign-off on basic flows. Next: finalize runbook and add a GitHub action to block merges if smoke tests regress. (Asha)
review_feedback: Maya: Request clearer failure messages from pre-upgrade hook; we updated logs to include failing pod names and reason codes
Lukas: Suggested adding a migration path for old prometheus PVC names; implemented name aliasing and a check to prevent accidental volume deletion
Priya: Asked for a minimal manifest render mode for air-gapped installs — added --render-manifests flag to the module examples
risks: Stateful Prometheus upgrades can cause metric gaps if not drained properly
Customer clusters with strict PodSecurityPolicies may need extra RBAC bindings — documented as pre-req
High-volume log pipelines may require tuned buffering; default config is conservative but may increase cost
follow_up_tasks: ENG-358220 - add performance benchmarks for logship under heavy load
ENG-358221 - add Grafana provisioning templates and dashboard imports
ENG-358222 - run 3 customer pilots and capture upgrade telemetry
notes: Implementation uses a small sidecar helper image to run pre-upgrade probes and emit structured events to our audit log
We intentionally avoid opinionated scrape rules for customer apps; instead we provide a recommended set that platform integrators can import
Module exposes outputs: grafana_url, prometheus_remote_write_endpoint, otlp_endpoint, logship_endpoint
